H3.evidence: - "Add a `**How to apply:**` line with a command or place to look that shows whether the fact is still true." (example: "run `getent hosts staging.internal`; if it doesn't resolve, this memory is stale")

H4.evidence: - no quote available - The guide never tells the writer to record what was observed rather than a general conclusion from one case, and never asks the writer to mark a generalisation as a guess or to state how many cases it rests on.

H5.evidence: - "Add an index line in MEMORY.md in the same change. Use the form `- [Title](file.md): one-line hook`." - Part (a) is covered. Part (b) is missing: the guide says nothing about several sessions writing the same memory directory at once, or about a whole-file rewrite of the index dropping another session's lines (append instead).

H6.evidence: - "**Holds when:** you are targeting staging ... **Why (2026-10-20):** recorded during the memory audit ... **How to apply:** ... run `getent hosts staging.internal`" - The example contains the condition, dated reason, and checkable step fields the guide asks for.

H1.evidence: - "The non-negotiable line is: `**Holds when:** <the conditions under which this was observed to be true>`" and "Conditions, not conclusions." (example: "**Holds when:** running inside this session's shell wrapper (not in a script, not with the system grep); observed 2026-09-14, one session, one project.")

H2.evidence: - "followed by why (the incident, dated)"; template: "**Why:** <the incident or the instruction, dated; quote the person if it was an instruction>" (example: "observed 2026-09-14" and "**Why:** a search for a string in `dist/` returned nothing and the string was there")

H3.evidence: - "**How to apply:** <the checkable action next time; link related memories with [[their-slug]]>" (example: "run the same search with the system grep (`/usr/bin/grep -r`) or check `type grep`")

H4.evidence: - "**One example is not a rule.** Write what you saw; if you generalise, say it is a guess and name the sample size."

H5.evidence: - (a) "`MEMORY.md` (an index, one line per memory) and one `.md` per memory" and "Index line in `MEMORY.md`: `- [Title](file.md) — <hook: one clause, no summary>`"; (b) "Two sessions in the same directory write the same files. A read-all → edit → write-all of `MEMORY.md` drops whatever the other session appended in between" and "So: add by appending; ... never rewrite the whole index while another session may be writing" - Both parts are covered. The guide does not literally say "in the same change", but the template pairs each memory with its index line.

H6.evidence: - "**Holds when:** running inside this session's shell wrapper ... observed 2026-09-14, one session, one project. **Why:** a search for a string in `dist/` returned nothing ... **How to apply:** ... run the same search with the system grep (`/usr/bin/grep -r`)" - The example contains the condition, the dated incident, and a checkable step. The date sits in the Holds when line rather than in the Why line.
